body.statement: For the standard-normal link, every comparable-rarity triangular array satisfying \(r_{\ell j,n}=\rho_n c_{\ell j,n}\), \(c_{\ell j,n}\in[1/2,4]\), and \(\rho_n\to0\) obeys \(\max_{1\le\ell\le L,\,j\in J}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))\to0\). Hence no constant \(C<\infty\) can make \(\inf_{\ell,j,n}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))\ge1/C\), so Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumption 5 excludes the entire comparable-rarity sequence rather than merely failing at an exact zero cell.
body.justification: This locates the rare experiment outside the published interior theorem by the exact regularity inequality used in that theorem.
body.gap: Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumption 5 states the positive link-density lower bound; this proposition records its direct implication for the comparable-rarity array and carries no independent novelty claim.
body.consumer: The Gaussian and product-Poisson frontier statements can be read as boundary results on a domain that the published weak-convergence theorem does not cover.
